_comment: Hand-curated layer of docs/capabilities.json (capability-config.md §2 p.3). The emitter (stapel_docs/_capabilities.py) merges this over the derived axes; an axis present in conf.py DEFAULTS but missing here (or vice versa) is a loud emission error. Keep business_label/summary in business language — they surface in CTO conversations, not in code. The one axis is composite: the emitter expresses axes as top-level DEFAULTS keys only, so the nested SHARING behavior knobs (MODES / LINK.ANONYMOUS / LINK.MAX_LEVEL / LINK.TTL_DAYS) surface as ONE `SHARING` axis whose default is the closed dict, not as per-key axes — the per-key story lives in the summary and in checks.py (E010-E013). `surface_roots` + `surface` are the third section (stapel_tools.surface): the usage surface — the symbols a host or a sibling module is meant to CALL instead of writing its own. The roots are scopes, not lists, so every public module-level function in a rooted file MUST carry an intent line here or emission fails naming it. Deliberately NOT rooted: events.py (the service layer emits document.* inside its own mutating transactions — host code that emits them double-publishes a public event), functions.py/actions.py (comm surface, reached by name over the bus, never imported), checks.py (Django check callbacks, invoked by the check framework), presenters.py (the view layer's DTO discipline; hosts reach it through the PRESENTERS swap keys documented as an extension point, not by calling the builders).
provides: Google-Drive-style workspace documents: a folder tree, one-entity-per-type documents over an open type registry, content-addressed snapshot storage with an update journal and revision history, optimistic-lock editing (v1), trash with irreversible purge, a swappable object-storage seam, comm ingest (docs.create_document) and registry-driven export (PDF built in).

requires.reason: comm bus (docs.create_document Function, document.* Actions, the workspaces.check_capability client), JWT authentication, unified error envelope, GDPR provider registry, AppSettings config layer

every HTTP authorization asks the workspaces.check_capability comm Function (fail-closed, deny-by-default) — stapel-workspaces is the shelf's answerer; any provider of that Function satisfies the contract, and without one every HTTP request denies (comm ingest still works)
every endpoint requires an authenticated non-anonymous user (IsNotAnonymousUser); stapel-auth is the shelf's session issuer — any stapel-core-compatible JWT issuer satisfies the check

extension_points.name: STORAGE
extension_points.summary: Swap the object-storage backend (DocsStorage implementation, REPLACE): any Django storage by default, bundled S3/MinIO backend ([s3] extra), or your own. Every byte of document content I/O goes through it — there is no second I/O path.

extension_points.name: DOC_TYPES
extension_points.summary: Open document-type registry ({slug: dotted-path to a DocTypeSpec | None to remove}, merged over the txt/md/csv/file builtins) or register at runtime via register_doc_type(). A type carries its editor hint, write discipline (snapshot|crdt), mime, empty body and text extractor — sheet/slides/office are later registry entries, not schema changes.

extension_points.name: EXPORTERS
extension_points.summary: Export-format registry ({format: dotted-path | None}, merged over the built-in pdf). An exporter renders (document, body, spec) to (bytes, mime) — add docx/html/srt without touching the module.

extension_points.name: INGEST
extension_points.summary: Event-driven ingest ({action_name: dotted-path mapper}): docs subscribes to the named host actions and routes each payload through the mapper into create_document — the host never writes a bus subscriber, and docs never learns a foreign event schema.

extension_points.name: SHARING_RESOLVERS
extension_points.summary: SHARING['RESOLVERS'] ({ref_kind: dotted-path}) — the whitelist subject-reference resolver registry. A resolver is a point query, resolve(ref, user_id) -> bool: the host answers 'is this person in that container' from its own data or a comm call, and docs never imports the source module or copies its membership. Fail-closed on both boundaries: an unregistered kind is refused at MINT (no dead rows), and an unknown kind or a raising resolver denies at READ.

extension_points.name: PRESENTERS
extension_points.summary: Every DTO is built by a presenter resolved through STAPEL_SWAP — swap keys DOCS_FOLDER_PRESENTER / DOCS_DOCUMENT_PRESENTER / DOCS_REVISION_PRESENTER reshape the folder/document/revision envelopes of every endpoint without forking a view.

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: Every view declares request/response serializer seams (SerializerSeamMixin) — subclass the view, override the attribute, remount the URL.

SHARING.summary: Composite axis over STAPEL_DOCS['SHARING']: MODES (additional grant sources, subset of whitelist|link), RESOLVERS (subject-reference resolvers), LINK.ANONYMOUS, LINK.MAX_LEVEL and LINK.TTL_DAYS. Both grant sources are IMPLEMENTED since 0.6.0 and the axis still ships CLOSED (MODES=[], no anonymous links, view ceiling, 30-day TTL): a host opens it deliberately, one settings line, and configuring what this version does not sanction is a loud system-check error (stapel_docs.E010-E014), never a silent no-op.
SHARING.behavior: Grant sources are additive and monotonic over the immutable workspace baseline: each is an independent sufficient reason, the composition is a union with the maximum level, so enabling a mode can only ever grant and disabling one can only ever inert its own rows (they are shown as suspended, never hidden). 'manage' is never grantable by any share source (anti-escalation invariant), an anonymous presenter never writes whatever level their link carries, and a link dies the moment its creator loses docs.share.link — checked live, with an outage answering 503 rather than a fabricated verdict.

authorize.intent: THE access decision for anything document-shaped — HTTP, presigned URLs, a future realtime stream. Returns allow|deny|unavailable (503, never 403-on-outage); fail-closed via workspaces.check_capability by comm name. Every new read or write path routes through this — a second membership check is how a share mode later ships half-enforced.

effective_spec.intent: The document's DocTypeSpec, or None when the type vanished from the registry — the degrade-to-file signal. Read specs through this per document rather than get_doc_type(), which raises on the vanished-type case the API deliberately survives.

content_mime.intent: The Content-Type a body must be served with: the spec's mime (+charset for text) for editable types, the stored original's for file/vanished types. Hand-picking a mime per call site is how a utf-8 markdown body ships as latin-1.

get_live_document.intent: Fetch a non-trashed document or raise the 404-mapped DocsError — the lookup every normal endpoint starts with (trashed rows are 404 outside the trash surface).

get_trashed_document.intent: Fetch a trashed document or 404 — only restore/purge flows see trashed rows.

get_live_folder.intent: Fetch a non-trashed folder or 404, optionally pinned to a workspace — the workspace pin is what stops a cross-workspace folder_id from being honored.

get_trashed_folder.intent: Fetch a trashed folder or 404 — the restore/purge counterpart of get_live_folder.

get_revision.intent: Fetch one revision of a given document or 404 — scoped through document.revisions so a revision id can never be read across documents.

get_upload_session.intent: Fetch an upload session by id or 404 — the finalize endpoint's lookup.

list_folders.intent: Live folders of a workspace — whole tree, workspace roots (parent_id=None) or one folder's children. The one listing that respects soft-deletion.

create_folder.intent: Mint a folder under the depth limit with live-sibling name uniqueness enforced in code (SQL cannot compare NULL parents). A bare Folder.objects.create skips both invariants.

rename_folder.intent: Rename with the sibling-name check — the same duplicate-name refusal creation applies.

move_folder.intent: Re-parent a folder with cycle, depth (subtree height counted) and sibling-name checks — the three ways a hand-written parent assignment corrupts the tree.

trash_folder.intent: Soft-delete the whole live subtree, documents included, announcing each document.deleted in the same transaction. Setting deleted_at by hand strands live documents inside a trashed tree.

restore_folder.intent: Untrash a subtree; restored documents are re-announced via document.created so downstream indexes come back consistent.

list_documents.intent: Live documents of a workspace (folder/type/title-substring filters), with pending uploads excluded — the invariant a raw queryset forgets, leaking half-uploaded rows into listings.

create_document.intent: THE document mint — HTTP, the docs.create_document Function and the INGEST seam all land here. Refuses unknown types loudly, materializes folder_path idempotently, rides the initial body through the regular snapshot path and announces document.created in the same transaction.

update_document.intent: Patch title/metadata — and strip the reserved upload-pending marker no caller outside the upload flow may set.

move_document.intent: Move a document to a folder (or the workspace root), with the target folder resolved live and workspace-pinned.

trash_document.intent: Soft-delete one document, emitting document.deleted inside the transaction — consumers learn it left the visible corpus.

restore_document.intent: Untrash one document, re-announced via document.created.

read_content.intent: (body, mime, head_seq) of the current head — the spec's empty body at seq 0 before any save. The only sanctioned body read; get_bytes on a guessed key bypasses the empty-body and vanished-type semantics.

storage_transaction.intent: Wrap a mutation whose object-store effects must follow the database outcome: writes are compensated when the block fails, deletes wait for the commit. Calling put_bytes/delete_object inside a transaction instead is how a rollback leaves an orphan object — or worse, deletes bytes a surviving row still points at.

resource_limit.intent: Read one integer ceiling out of the STAPEL_DOCS namespace (0 = that ceiling is off). Host code that hardcodes a byte limit ships a number the operator cannot tune and the audit cannot find.

assert_body_size.intent: Refuse a snapshot body above MAX_BODY_BYTES (413). Every path that accepts client bytes calls it before touching storage — a body checked after the write has already cost the store.

assert_body_mutable.intent: Refuse a generic body write to a type that owns its own write path: file bodies come from an upload session (where size/MIME/quota policy lives) and a vanished type is read-only. Skipping it re-opens the content PUT as a second, unpoliced door into blob bodies.

workspace_usage_bytes.intent: Stored bytes charged to a workspace (heads + revision snapshots) — the figure the quota compares against and the one to show in a usage UI.

assert_quota.intent: Refuse a write that would push the workspace past WORKSPACE_QUOTA_BYTES (507). Call it before accepting bytes, not after storing them.

pending_uploads.intent: Open (pending, unexpired) upload sessions of a workspace — the set the per-workspace ceiling counts and the one a cleanup job should sweep.

save_content.intent: The optimistic-lock snapshot save: expected_seq is checked under select_for_update, the snapshot is content-addressed, an auto revision is minted on the configured cadence, the orphaned previous snapshot dies, the journal compacts, and document.updated + document.storage_changed leave in the same transaction. There is exactly one save path — restore and create-with-body use it too.

append_updates.intent: Append opaque commutative updates (crdt-discipline types only) at ++head_seq each, with client_id/client_seq retry dedup. Journal appends deliberately do NOT emit document.updated (bus economy).

read_updates.intent: The replay feed since a sequence number, with honest resync semantics: a since that fell out of the compaction window returns ("resync", None) instead of a silently incomplete list.

assemble_crdt_snapshot.intent: Materialize a yjs-codec document's update journal into its snapshot: fold via pycrdt, snapshot_seq catches up to head_seq WITHOUT minting a seq, auto revision + compaction + document.updated ride the same storage path as every save. Triggered from append_updates past CRDT_ASSEMBLE_UPDATE_INTERVAL and by the idle beat sweep; call directly to force a fold. No-op (None) for non-yjs types.

assert_crdt_body.intent: Refuse a snapshot body or journal payload that does not parse as a Y update, for codec="yjs" types only (400 error.400.docs_invalid_crdt_payload). The write-door guard that keeps a text body from corrupting the crdt discipline; snapshot and host-codec types pass through untouched.

create_named_revision.intent: Name the CURRENT head snapshot; naming the same head twice renames the existing named revision instead of stacking rows.

revision_content.intent: A revision's FULL bytes — every revision is a self-contained snapshot (I1), so one get_bytes suffices; no delta chain to walk.

restore_revision.intent: Restore-as-new-head: the revision's bytes ride the same save path as a PUT (always minting a revision), so history is never rewritten. Copying bytes onto the row by hand loses the revision trail and the storage accounting.

trash_listing.intent: Everything soft-deleted in a workspace — (folders, documents) for the trash surface.

purge_document.intent: Irreversible destruction of one document: every distinct storage key of its history + journal + rows, O(document), idempotent, with document.deleted and the negative byte delta announced inside the transaction. Deleting the row alone leaks every object its history points at.

purge_folder.intent: Purge a trashed folder with its trashed contents; live documents still pointing into the subtree survive at the workspace root (FK SET_NULL), never destroyed by a folder purge.

empty_trash.intent: Purge the listed trashed items — or the whole workspace trash. A non-trashed or unknown id refuses the WHOLE request: partial purges are how a client deletes more than the user confirmed.

purge_expired.intent: Retention expiry: purge everything soft-deleted longer than TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS ago — the body of the docs_purge_expired management command; call it from a host cron/beat instead of re-deriving the cutoff.

create_upload.intent: Open an upload session (type=file): the Document row exists immediately but stays hidden from listings until finalize, and the ticket's key/TTL are what finalize later validates. put_url is storage-presigned when the backend accepts a direct PUT, else the module's own signed intake URL — a bare presigned_put_url gives you neither the choice nor the ticket.

receive_upload_bytes.intent: Store a client's upload body for its session (the module-intake PUT's server half): pending + unexpired + under MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES, then put_bytes under the ticket's key. Declared-size/checksum verdicts stay finalize's — a raw put_bytes skips even these ticket checks.

upload_intake_signer.intent: The TimestampSigner (dedicated salt) behind module-intake put_urls — the signature is the whole credential of the intake PUT. Verify or mint intake signatures through it or the ticket and the URL stop agreeing.

finalize_upload.intent: Promote the uploaded object to the document's first version (HEAD-verified size, seq 1, first revision, pending marker cleared) and announce document.created + the byte delta. Emitting the events yourself skips every one of those steps.

download_url.intent: Presigned GET URL for a stored object key with the configured lifetime — opaque to clients; DjangoStorageBackend degrades it to a served URL, so never assume S3 URL shape.

content_hash.intent: The sha256 content address of a body — the identity under which snapshots dedup. Any custom write path hashes through this or dedup silently stops.

document_prefix.intent: The object-key prefix every object of a document lives under ({STORAGE_PREFIX}/{workspace}/{document}) — what makes purge O(document) and byte accounting per-workspace. Keys built outside it escape both.

snapshot_key.intent: The content-addressed snapshot key for a body hash — identical bodies collapse to one stored object for free.

blob_key.intent: A content-addressed key with an extension hint, for auxiliary blobs a custom flow stores next to a document under the same prefix discipline.

get_storage.intent: THE object-store handle for anything touching document bytes — the configured DocsStorage (Django default_storage, the bundled S3/MinIO backend, or the host's own), memoized. An export script or admin action goes through this rather than building its own boto3 client: the STORAGE seam makes the bucket, credentials and presign policy one decision instead of one per call site.

reset_storage_cache.intent: Drop the memoized backend so the next get_storage() re-resolves the STORAGE setting — the supported way to make an override_settings block take effect. Overwhelmingly a test-harness concern.

register_doc_type.intent: Register (or replace) a document type at runtime — the programmatic equivalent of the DOC_TYPES settings overlay for apps that register from AppConfig.ready(). Mutating BUILTIN_DOC_TYPES reaches the same map from the wrong side and loses to the overlay.

unregister_doc_type.intent: Remove one runtime registration — the teardown that stops one test's type from leaking into the next.

get_doc_types.intent: The effective {slug: DocTypeSpec} registry — builtins, then the DOC_TYPES overlay, then runtime registrations. Render type pickers and dispatch editors from this; BUILTIN_DOC_TYPES answers only "which types shipped".

get_doc_type.intent: One slug's spec, or DocTypeNotRegistered — the loud lookup for flows that must refuse an unknown type (ingest does). For presentation of existing rows use effective_spec, which degrades instead of raising.

get_exporter.intent: Instantiate the exporter registered for a format (builtins + EXPORTERS overlay) or raise ExportFormatUnknown — the dispatch any custom export endpoint or batch job goes through.

with_stars.intent: Annotate is_starred on a Folder/Document queryset for one user — None (not False) when there is no user, because 'not applicable' and 'not starred' are different answers. Reach for it in any custom listing that presents docs rows; hand-writing the Exists() subquery is how the anonymous case silently becomes False.

attach_star.intent: Set is_starred on a single already-fetched Folder/Document — the detail-envelope counterpart of with_stars, for rows a queryset annotation can no longer reach.

set_star.intent: Star or unstar one document/folder for one user, idempotently; returns whether anything changed. The only supported writer of the Star table — a direct create() skips the exactly-one-target contract the endpoint relies on.

starred_listing.intent: (folders, documents) one user starred in a workspace, live rows only — trashed items drop out of the listing but keep their star until purge, so a restore brings the bookmark back.

touch_recent.intent: Record that a user just reached a document (upsert + per-user trim). Call it from any NEW read path you add over document bytes; the shipped paths (content read, download-URL issuance, accepted save) already do.

recent_documents.intent: Documents one user reached most recently in a workspace, newest first, live only — the read side of the recents surface.

search.intent: Workspace-scoped name search over live folders and documents, returning (kind, row, breadcrumb) triples with ancestor chains resolved in one query. Use it instead of two icontains queries plus a parent walk — the walk is the N+1 this function exists to avoid.

workspace_usage.intent: Everything docs.usage reports for one workspace: live/trash/total bytes, item counts and a per-type breakdown. bytes_total is the same sum the 507 quota refuses against, so a meter and a refusal can never disagree. Host billing composes an entitlement ceiling from it; docs owns the measurement, never the price.

get_thumbnail.intent: (image bytes, mime) for an image file document at a fixed tier — renders once through Pillow, caches under the document's own storage prefix and registers the object so purge takes it along. 503-mapped when Pillow is absent, 400 for a non-image or an unknown tier.

thumbnail_key.intent: Storage key of a cached thumbnail, carrying head_seq so a saved document addresses a different image instead of a stale cache. Read it to reason about the bucket; get_thumbnail is what writes it.

document_download_url.intent: Mint a download URL for a document's current body AND record the reach in recents — the document-level wrapper of download_url, which stays the raw key-level mint for revisions.

render.intent: Resize image bytes so the longest edge fits a tier, as JPEG (alpha composited onto white, never upscaled). Raises ThumbnailsUnavailable without Pillow and ThumbnailSourceUnusable for bytes it cannot decode — a caller's bad input is a 400, not a 500.

available.intent: Is the thumbnail renderer installed? For host diagnostics and system checks that want to say so at deploy time instead of at the first 503.

granted_level.intent: The MAXIMUM level the enabled grant sources give one principal on one document, plus an outage flag — the same number authorize() decided with. Present so the presentation layer never re-derives 'what may this bearer do': a second answer to that question is how a share mode ships half-enforced.

check_share_capability.intent: allow|deny|unavailable for docs.share.whitelist / docs.share.link — who may GIVE access. Deliberately outside authorize()'s action vocabulary: minting a grant is a workspace mandate, not a level on the document, and conflating them turns 'shared with me' into 'may share with others'.

sharing_settings.intent: The effective SHARING dict with closed defaults merged in (never a partial overlay). Read the axis through this, not settings.STAPEL_DOCS — a half-merged LINK sub-dict is how ANONYMOUS silently reads as absent rather than False.

effective_modes.intent: Grant sources actually in force: deployment MODES ∩ what this version implements (∩ per-workspace narrowing once workspaces exposes settings). The one place the axis is read, so a mode can never be enabled by a code path that forgot to filter.

mode_enabled.intent: Kill-switch predicate for one mode. The share sheet marks rows of a disabled mode 'suspended' with it — never hides them, because an admin who cannot see an inert grant believes it was revoked.

link_settings.intent: SHARING['LINK'] with its closed defaults merged in (ANONYMOUS/MAX_LEVEL/TTL_DAYS) — the two locks on the leakiest door, read in one place.

ref_kind.intent: The resolver-registry key of a subject reference: everything before the LAST colon ('chat:conversation:<id>' -> 'chat:conversation'). One rule at every namespacing depth, so a host's registered key is exactly what it wrote.

get_ref_resolver.intent: The registered SHARING['RESOLVERS'] callable for a ref kind, or None. An unregistered kind and an unimportable path answer the same way — nothing to ask — and the caller turns that into deny.

resolve_ref.intent: Point-query a host resolver: is this user a member of this external container? Fail-closed on every unhappy path (unknown kind, raising resolver), answers cached ~30 s so revocation in the container reaches the document in seconds rather than never. Never copy a foreign module's membership instead of calling this.

may_write.intent: Whether a principal may ever author a write. An anonymous presenter never writes, whatever level their link carries: the journal and revision history are attributed by design, and an authorless edit is vandalism with no subject to name.

mark_sharing_suspended.intent: Stamp is_suspended on share-sheet rows whose mode is switched off. The kill-switch is a display state, not a filter: rows stay listed so an operator can see and revoke what a re-enabled mode would restore.

list_access.intent: Whitelist grants of one document, newest first, already marked suspended when the mode is off.

grant_access.intent: Create or raise one whitelist grant (upsert — re-granting is the sheet's ordinary gesture). Refuses a disabled mode, an unknown level, a half-named subject, and a ref whose kind has no registered resolver: a row that could only ever deny is never stored. Emits document.share.granted in the mutating transaction.

get_access.intent: One grant of THIS document or a 404-mapped DocsError — scoped by document, so an id from another workspace addresses nothing.

revoke_access.intent: Delete one whitelist grant and emit document.share.revoked. Works while the mode is off: taking access away must never be the thing nobody is allowed to do.

list_links.intent: Bearer links of one document, newest first, marked suspended when link sharing is off. The envelope carries live tokens — gate the caller on docs.share.link.

link_expiry.intent: The deadline a link minted now would carry (LINK['TTL_DAYS']). TTL_DAYS=None means perpetual and becomes a century, not a null: the column is NOT NULL by the invitation canon, and a date every reader renders beats an absence every reader special-cases.

create_link.intent: Mint one bearer link (secrets.token_urlsafe, mandatory expiry, level ≤ LINK['MAX_LEVEL'] refused loudly rather than clamped). Emits document.share.link_created. The second cap — never above the granter's own level — is applied by the caller through authorize().

get_link.intent: One link of THIS document or a 404-mapped DocsError.

revoke_link.intent: Withdraw a bearer link; idempotent (an already-revoked link keeps its first revoked_at and emits once). Revocation is terminal — revoked beats expired beats active, and a revoked link never revives.

get_link_by_token.intent: Resolve a presented token to (document, link), 404 when it names nothing. Liveness and level are decided by authorize(), never here — and the bearer views render every refusal as 404 so the endpoint is not an oracle for guessing tokens.

redeem_link.intent: Stamp first_redeemed_at once and emit document.share.link_redeemed. Call only AFTER authorize() allowed the request: the stamp is evidence somebody got in, so a refused presentation must not write it. Guarded by a conditional UPDATE, so two simultaneous first openings emit exactly one event.
